$comment: JRM Studio manifest. Source of truth for the cross-repo sync engine in sync/ (see docs/sync.md and sync/README.md), which reads this file on every run. Fields fall into three tiers. EXECUTED — repo, optIn.base, optIn.agents/skills/prompts/instructions, targetPaths and tokens decide which files are written where; getting one wrong changes the output. VERIFIED — mode selects the checkout evidence contract; framework, packageManager and called backbone workflows are checked when they apply but never decide a write. RECORDED — localAgents names locally authored roles/replacements used for handoff validation but never copied; optIn.health and optIn.workflows are native kinds (sync/lib/manifest.mjs NATIVE_KINDS), so neither is copied. DESCRIPTIVE — notes supplies human/agent context. Schema validation covers mode, mode-specific facts, repo, optIn, localAgents and tokens; integrity validation also enforces canonical agent and prompt roster/dependency closure. Real syncs, --check, and --work-dir additionally inspect each existing member checkout, then fail that member before writes if its mode or registry claims disagree. Manifest-only --dry-run stays offline and cannot verify checkout facts. See sync/README.md#member-entries.

optInSyntax.$comment: Each member.optIn.<kind> is either the string "*" (all canon of that kind), an array of names, or false (opt out). base/health are booleans.

tokens.$comment: Vendored design tokens from the OTHER private backbone repo jrmoulckers/studio (package @jrm/tokens). Registry-free: the sync engine copies studio's committed dist/ tree verbatim into each opted-in member (Option A). The whole sourceBase tree is mirrored today; a future optional per-member `include` (array of sub-globs under sourceBase) may narrow this without a breaking schema change. Per-member opt-in lives in members[].tokens, kept separate from optIn because the source is an external repo, not the .github canon.

members.notes: New consumer web product. Adopts the full canonical layer.
Game-night scoring app. Adopts the canonical roster and keeps its committed design-engineer as an explicit local replacement, so only design-engineer is omitted from sync.
Product-specific platform and risk rules live in root/scoped overlays. The canonical AI layer is materialized atomically while finance-domain remains the only locally authored agent.
Pure-client media hub for books and audiobooks. Svelte/Vite PWA at repo root; first member to consume vendored @jrm/tokens.

Local-first game library PWA. Svelte 5 + Vite at repo root, IndexedDB via idb, vite-plugin-pwa. Separate bridge/ Cloudflare Worker (OAuth token exchange, KV cache, CORS allowlist) with its own toolchain, so this member is not backend-free. Opted in with "*": its partial canon set came from a hand-typed list in a scaffold script, not a curation decision, so freezing it would preserve a first-pass guess.

Native-first task system with a Svelte PWA, pnpm workspace, shared domain/contracts packages, Hono/SQLite server, and planned SwiftUI client. Upgraded from pre-bootstrap immediately when its application and root toolchain evidence landed.

Design and tooling kernel with local principles as the authoritative map for canonical roles. The AI layer is materialized without the broad, unpinned base agency.toml; Studio remains the token source, never its own vendored-token target.

Infrastructure-as-code and operations repository for Proxmox, self-hosted services, automation, backups, and runbooks. Its eight product-specific agents remain local alongside the canonical roster; base stays disabled to preserve local AGENTS and runtime/MCP policy. Its audited prompt subset is intentionally read-oriented: backlog, review, and the hardened audit-first cleanup.

Windows device-management repository for shared and per-machine configuration. The canonical AI layer is enabled under infrastructure evidence checks while base remains disabled for the intentionally empty/tooling repository.
